subject: infra.cybersec
name: Cybersecurity Regulations (LTA-REG-0013-2026)
milestone: Made by the LTA under the Telecommunications Act 2007, 13 January 2026, effective from the day of publication
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: Requires telecom providers to store personal data and PII primarily inside Liberia's own territory (s.7.3(A)(v)), establish an in-house Cybersecurity Unit within one year of the effective date (s.7.1), notify the LTA of breaches within 24 hours and customers within 72 hours (s.7.6(A)(ii)), run annual penetration testing and keep security-event logs for at least 12 months (s.7.5), and file tested incident-response and continuity plans; the LTA is to run a sector CERT with a 24/7 hotline (s.8.2). Penalties are revenue-linked (up to US$3,000 plus 0.15% of the preceding year's gross revenue for failing to establish the Unit, escalating to US$25,000 and possible licence suspension) but apply only from one year after the effective date (s.10.7); the s.10.6 penalty escalation ladder is unreadable in both held copies (2026-01)
note: The s.10.6 penalty ladder is mangled in the readable text capture and unrenderable from the regulator's own image-only scan; the 13 January 2026 date is the regulation's stated making-date, not independently confirmed as the publication date that fixes entry into force under s.12.1.
